newsitem.title: USA: Citation sees FY96 EPS below forecasts.
newsitem.headline: Citation sees FY96 EPS below forecasts.

text.p: Citation Corp said on Tuesday that its earnings per share for its fiscal year ending September 29 were expected to be about 15 to 20 percent below Wall Street analysts' forecasts.
The company said in a statement that the forecast was based on preliminary results and the performance was "due to an expected shortfall in its fiscal fourth quarter."
Despite the expected EPS shortfall, the company said it thought it would report record sales and earnings for fiscal 1996.

Citation reported $1.27 EPS on sales of $307.7 million and earnings of $17.1 million for fiscal 1995. Due to a secondary offering of about four million shares in September 1995, EPS is based on 17.7 million shares versus 13.4 million shares outstanding for fiscal 1995.

The shortfall, which would affect fourth quarter EPS, was caused by a combination of factors, including normal maintenance shutdowns of most divisions in July or August, continued slow progress of expansion iron casting production lines at the Texas Foundries division in Lufkin, Texas, the idling of a steel foundry at that same location, and equipment problems at the Iroquois Foundry division in Browntown, Wis.

In addition, the Mansfield Foundry division in Mansfield, Ohio lost money in part due to excessive inventory that reduced operating levels, the statement said. Further details were not immediately available.
